boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Second Kernstown record (July 24, 1864) in Early's Raid and Operations Against the B&O Railroad [June-August 1864]. The July 23 reconnaissance, the July 25 fighting at Martinsburg and the July 26 crossing of the Potomac are context. Campaign-wide marches, levies, captures, returns and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. Imported numerical estimates remain unchanged; this pass does not validate them as simultaneous opening forces.

claims.value: The frozen and live force fields read 23,000 total (US 10,000; CS 13,000); the source basis is not given. Crook says 3,000 or 4,000 of his dismounted cavalry and some infantry broke to the rear at the first fire, and that the attacking force was Early's raiding force joined by the troops left in the Valley. Pond says Crook's line held the divisions of Sullivan, Duval and Mulligan with Averell's and Duffie's cavalry on the flanks, and that the force later assembled to match Early was thrice Crook's at Kernstown. Pond quotes Crook's July 22 dispatch that he had not force sufficient to meet all the enemy in the open Valley.
claims.rationale: No inspected passage gives a count for either side on July 24; the imported figures are unvalidated. None is adopted as a matched opening strength.

claims.value: Crook says he gave the order to fall back when a column moved around his right. Pond says Early, seeing Crook's left assailable, directed Breckinridge to send Wharton's division against it, and that Ransom, ill, could not take active command of Early's cavalry. The frozen commanders are Lieutenant General Early and Brigadier General George Crook; Crook signs as brevet major general.
claims.rationale: Command roles from an interested report and a history; neither listed commander receives automatic sole credit.

Crook crossed the Potomac on the 26th.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 1,800 total (US 1,200; CS 600); the live field reads 1785 (US 1185; CS 600). Pond says Crook's loss could hardly have been less than 1,200, giving Duval's division 513, Hayes's brigade 396 and Mulligan's division 317, and says the Confederate loss was light. Mulligan was mortally wounded.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. The compiled Union return (No. 55) is garbled in OCR and was not selected; no Confederate figure was inspected.

open_questions: The compiled return No. 55 (garbled), Averell's July 30 report (read, not selected), Thoburn's, Duval's, Hayes's and the regimental reports, and all Confederate reports remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. George E. Pond's The Shenandoah Valley in 1864 (Scribner, 1883) is a retrospective history written, by its preface, from the official documents at the War Records Office and field despatches; it quotes the reports of the commanders it describes and is not independent of them. Crook's July 27 and October 12, 1864 reports, printed in Official Records Series I, Volume XXXVII, Part 1, are one family of interested Union accounts; Pond quotes them. The Official Records volumes are shared containers, not additional witnesses. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
